newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asiana takes to the water for Macau cargo service.
newsitem.headline: Asiana takes to the water for Macau cargo service.

text.p: Asiana Airlines has become the second airline to start shipping air cargo from Hong Kong to Macau by barge to feed its newly inaugurated freighter service to Seoul, Asiana's director of cargo marketing and sales, T.S.Kang told Reuters.
Asiana's newly delivered Boeing 767 freighter began flying to the Portuguese enclave, some 50 miles across the Pearl River estuary from Hong Kong on September 5.
Kang said that lack of slots at over-crowded Kai Tak airport was a major reason for starting the Macau service to supplement its Hong Kong flights.

Industry sources said the arrival of the South Korean carrier is a welcome boost for Macau airport which industry observers said has been struggling to attract airlines to fill capacity since it opened last November.
Scandinavian Airlines System said it was the first airline to pioneer the barge concept to transport air cargo from Hong Kong to Macau to feed its Macau-New Delhi-Gothenburg service.
Asiana said the barge is the "weak point" in its new service.

"It looks very very slow but it not so inferior to our service from Hong Kong. The barge service is efficient and the warehousing facilities at Macau are very good. I'm very happy and think we can compete with other airlines in Hong Kong from Macau," Kang said.
The Asiana cargo barge leaves Hong Kong at 1400 local time, arrives at Macau airport's warehouse between 2100-2300 and flies out the following morning to Seoul, Kang added.
Asiana now has two flights a week from Macau, a scheduled service on Thursdays and charter on Fridays.

"After we have evaluated the demand, I think ultimately we will have two permanent flights to Macau. Out of Macau the load factors are very good, for example last Friday's flight had 52 tonnes aboard for Seoul," Kang said.
But he says initial load factors into Macau are poor.
"Our customers in Korea are not familiar with Macau and they are quite reluctant at the moment so we have to convince them. I think we can do that," Kang said.

Asiana declined to reveal its pricing policy but say it is cheaper to fly cargo from Macau than Hong Kong. The Macau service complements Asiana's daily passenger flights plus two combi flights a week from Hong Kong.
Kang believes more airlines will also start flying into Macau.

"I personally think Macau will fundamentally change attitudes towards Hong Kong's new airport being built at Chek Lap Kok. I think the value of two airports remain important. Two can be more dynamic and I don't think airlines will pull out of Macau when Chek Lap Kok opens," he added.
